outlineVi: Mở đầu: Giới thiệu ngắn gọn về sự kiện bất ngờ khiến bản thân vỡ òa hạnh phúc (nhận email trúng tuyển học bổng du học khi tưởng chừng đã trượt).
Ý 1 (Khi nào, ở đâu): Diễn ra vào một buổi chiều mưa tại phòng riêng khoảng hai năm trước, lúc đang chuẩn bị tâm lý đón nhận thất bại.
Ý 2 (Người cùng chia sẻ): Bố mẹ ở nhà và người bạn thân; cảm xúc ôm chầm lấy mẹ trong nước mắt và gọi điện khoe bạn bè.
Kết (Lý do mang lại hạnh phúc to lớn): Không chỉ vì cơ hội học thuật mà còn là sự ghi nhận nỗ lực suốt nhiều tháng, đồng thời trút bỏ gánh nặng tài chính cho gia đình.
happiness.sample: I'd like to talk about an unexpected moment that truly made my day, which was when I received an acceptance letter for an overseas exchange programme about two years ago. It happened on a gloomy Tuesday afternoon while I was sitting alone in my bedroom. Honestly, I had convinced myself that I stood no chance because the competition was fierce, so I was bracing for rejection. But when I refreshed my inbox and saw the word 'Congratulations', I was utterly elated. My mother was preparing dinner downstairs, and the moment I rushed down shouting, she immediately burst into tears of relief. We hugged each other tightly, and shortly after, I called my best friend, who had reviewed countless essay drafts with me, to share the news. This event brought me immense happiness because it wasn't just a validation of my academic efforts after months of burning the midnight oil; it also relieved a tremendous financial burden off my parents' shoulders through a full tuition waiver. Experiencing such relief and pride alongside my loved ones created an enduring memory of sheer joy.

p1.q: What kinds of things make you feel happy in your daily life?
p1.a: For me, it is mostly small everyday pleasures, like sipping a freshly brewed coffee in the morning or sharing a laugh with colleagues. These simple rituals help relieve stress and ground me amidst my busy schedule.

p1.q: Do you think you were happier when you were a child than you are now?
p1.a: I would say yes. As a child, I enjoyed sheer carefree freedom without the weight of financial obligations or work pressure, whereas now, happiness requires more deliberate effort and a good work-life balance.

p1.q: What do you usually do when you want to cheer yourself up after a hard day?
p1.a: Whenever I feel drained, I usually go for a brisk jog or listen to upbeat acoustic music. Engaging in physical movement triggers endorphins, which almost immediately lifts my mood and clears my head.

p3.q: Do you believe that material wealth is essential for long-term happiness in modern society?
p3.a: While wealth provides basic financial security and access to healthcare, I don't believe it guarantees lasting fulfillment. Beyond a certain threshold, money merely fuels consumerism, as people quickly adapt to luxury through the hedonic treadmill. Conversely, genuine joy stems from meaningful relationships and personal growth. Therefore, money serves as a vital foundation, but emotional well-being is what truly sustains happiness.

p3.q: How has the way people define happiness changed compared to previous generations?
p3.a: In the past, happiness was closely tied to communal stability, raising a family, and securing permanent employment. Nowadays, however, younger generations prioritize individual self-actualization, mental wellness, and unique experiences like global travel. While our grandparents valued duty and social conformity, modern individuals tend to seek authenticity and autonomy, redefining happiness as a deeply personal journey rather than a societal checklist.

mistakesVi: Lạm dụng lặp từ 'happy' hoặc 'very happy' thay vì sử dụng đa dạng các từ vựng band điểm cao hơn như 'content', 'thrilled', 'overjoyed' hay 'on cloud nine'.
Nhầm lẫn từ loại giữa danh từ 'happiness' và tính từ 'happy', hoặc dùng sai giới từ phổ biến (ví dụ nói 'happy with' khi nói về sự kiện thay vì 'happy about').
Trong Part 3, thí sinh có thói quen trả lời quá cảm tính và mang tính cá nhân ('I feel happy when...') thay vì phân tích ở bình diện vĩ mô, xã hội hoặc tâm lý học con người.

outlineVi: Mở đầu: Giới thiệu thói quen lành mạnh (uống 2 lít nước mỗi ngày) và mốc thời gian bắt đầu (khoảng một năm trước do cơ thể hay mệt mỏi).
Ý 1: Cách thức duy trì thói quen trong cuộc sống bận rộn (dùng bình nước có vạch chia thời gian, cài ứng dụng nhắc nhở trên điện thoại).
Ý 2: Những khó khăn ban đầu gặp phải (sự lười biếng, thường xuyên quên, bất tiện khi phải đi vệ sinh nhiều lần) và cách vượt qua.
Kết: Những chuyển biến tích cực rõ rệt về thể chất và tinh thần (da sáng hơn, hết đau đầu, nhiều năng lượng) cùng quyết tâm duy trì lâu dài.
health.sample: I'd like to talk about a habit I've been cultivating over the past year, which is drinking at least two liters of water every single day. I picked up this habit early last year when I started feeling constantly fatigued and suffering from frequent headaches. My doctor pointed out that mild dehydration was the culprit and advised me to increase my daily fluid intake. To keep this up consistently, I bought a large reusable water bottle with time markings on the side, which reminds me when to sip. I also installed a hydration tracker app on my phone that buzzes every hour. In the beginning, it felt tedious to constantly refill my bottle, but after a few weeks, it became second nature. This simple change has truly worked wonders for my health. Not only has my skin cleared up significantly, but my afternoon brain fog has also vanished. I feel far more energized throughout the day and rarely experience tension headaches anymore. Sticking to this routine has really shown me how small daily changes yield huge health rewards.

p1.q: How do you keep healthy?
p1.a: To stay in good shape, I prioritize a balanced diet and regular physical activity. For instance, I cook fresh meals at home with plenty of vegetables and make sure to jog for at least thirty minutes every other morning.

p1.q: Do you exercise regularly?
p1.a: Yes, I make it a point to work out three or four times a week. I usually alternate between cardio sessions and light strength training at my local gym, which keeps my energy levels high throughout the working week.

p1.q: What do usually eat for breakfast?
p1.a: I typically go for something light yet nutritious, such as a bowl of oatmeal topped with fresh bananas and walnuts. It provides sustained energy and keeps me full until lunchtime without causing sluggishness.

p3.q: Should governments pay more for public health services?
p3.a: In my view, governments should definitely allocate a larger portion of their budget to public healthcare. Affordable medical services ensure that vulnerable populations receive essential treatments without falling into severe medical debt. While some argue that this strains public finances, preventative care ultimately reduces long-term economic burdens caused by widespread chronic diseases. Therefore, investing in robust healthcare systems benefits society as a whole.

p3.q: Why do many people find it hard to build healthy habits?
p3.a: I think modern lifestyles are the primary culprit. People often juggle demanding work hours and family responsibilities, which leaves them physically drained and prone to choosing quick comfort, like junk food, over exercising. Furthermore, healthy habits require instant effort for delayed gratification, whereas scrolling social media or snacking offers immediate pleasure. Without strong discipline, it is remarkably easy to fall back into unhealthy routines.

mistakesVi: Lạm dụng từ 'healthy': Người học thường lặp lại tính từ này liên tục (healthy food, healthy body, healthy habit). Nên linh hoạt dùng 'wholesome diet', 'nutritious meals', 'stay in shape', hoặc 'physical well-being'.
Dùng sai từ loại giữa 'health' (danh từ) và 'healthy' (tính từ): Điển hình là lỗi nói 'improve my healthy' thay vì 'improve my health', hoặc 'take care of my healthy'.
Dùng sai cụm 'play exercise' hoặc 'play gym': Trong tiếng Anh không dùng động từ 'play' cho việc tập thể dục nói chung. Cần dùng 'do exercise', 'work out', hoặc 'hit the gym'.

hobbies.sample:
About six months ago, I decided to take up pottery making, which has surprisingly become my favorite pastime. I first stumbled upon it while watching an artisanal craft documentary on YouTube, and seeing the potter transform wet clay into elegant ceramics completely captivated me. I signed up for a beginner workshop at a local studio the very next weekend.

Nowadays, I carve out three hours every Saturday morning to attend studio sessions. During these classes, I practice wheel throwing and hand-building techniques, crafting simple items like coffee mugs and small plant pots.

This hobby has become deeply meaningful to me for a couple of key reasons. Firstly, it offers a wonderful creative outlet away from digital screens. Working with my hands requires absolute concentration, which helps me completely lose track of time and blow off steam after stressful workweeks. More importantly, pottery has taught me patience; clay is unforgiving, and when a pot collapses, you simply have to center yourself and begin anew. Taking home a finished, glazed cup that I crafted with my own hands gives me an immense sense of fulfillment.

p1.q: Do you have any hobbies that you prefer doing alone rather than with others?
p1.a: Definitely. I really enjoy sketching architectural buildings in my sketchbook by myself. It requires deep focus, and being alone allows me to immerse myself fully in the process without feeling self-conscious or distracted by conversation.

p1.q: Did you spend your leisure time differently when you were a child?
p1.a: Yes, quite drastically. As a kid, I spent countless hours playing traditional street games with neighborhood friends, whereas nowadays my downtime revolves around solitary indoor pastimes like reading or listening to podcasts after tiring workdays.

p1.q: Is there a new hobby or creative pursuit you would like to take up soon?
p1.a: I would love to learn sourdough baking in the coming months. Crafting naturally fermented bread seems incredibly satisfying, and I really want to master the art of kneading dough to make fresh breakfasts at home.

p3.q: Why do some people find it difficult to maintain a regular hobby in modern society?
p3.a: In my opinion, the frantic pace of modern life is the main culprit. Many professionals juggle heavy workloads with domestic chores, leaving little mental energy for personal pursuits. Moreover, the prevalence of smartphones tempts people into passive entertainment like scrolling social media rather than actively cultivating a hobby. Consequently, meaningful leisure activities are often sidelined due to sheer cognitive fatigue and lack of disciplined schedule management.

p3.q: To what extent can hobbies influence an individual's personal or professional growth?
p3.a: I believe personal pastimes have a profound impact on one's development. Engaging in team sports or strategy games fosters critical soft skills like teamwork, problem-solving, and adaptability, which directly translate to the workplace. Furthermore, creative hobbies like painting or photography promote lateral thinking and emotional resilience. While some view leisure as unproductive downtime, it actually builds a well-rounded mindset that enhances professional competence over the long run.

mistakesVi: Dịch nghĩa đen 'chơi sở thích' thành 'play a hobby' (sai ngữ pháp); cần dùng 'take up a hobby', 'pursue a pastime' hoặc 'engage in a leisure activity'.
Lặp lại từ 'hobby' quá nhiều lần trong một câu trả lời thay vì linh hoạt dùng các từ đồng nghĩa như 'recreational activity', 'pursuit', 'downtime' hoặc 'pastime'.
Kể tên những thói quen thụ động đơn thuần như 'sleeping' hay 'surfing Facebook' như một hobby thực thụ mà thiếu đi sự phân tích về mục đích, kỹ năng hoặc giá trị tinh thần.

hometown.sample:
A place in my hometown that I absolutely love visiting is West Lake, which is situated just a short ride north of Hanoi's bustling city center. It is an expansive freshwater lake surrounded by scenic tree-lined paths and lively open-air cafes.

Whenever I go there, there are plenty of enjoyable things to do. I usually like renting a bicycle to ride along the shoreline and feel the refreshing breeze, or simply grabbing an iced coffee with close friends at a lakeside cafe while watching the sunset paint the sky.

I tend to visit on weekend late afternoons, especially around dusk, because that is when the intense daytime heat subsides and the atmosphere turns genuinely tranquil. Occasionally, on exhausting weekdays, I also take a solitary stroll there in the evening to clear my head.

I truly cherish this spot because it provides a peaceful sanctuary away from the relentless traffic and chaos of the capital. The open water creates a rare sense of spaciousness, which helps me recharge my batteries and reflect on life.

p1.q: Where is your hometown?
p1.a: I was born and raised in Da Nang, a coastal city situated in central Vietnam. It is widely renowned for its scenic beaches like My Khe and iconic bridges stretching across the Han River.

p1.q: What do you like most about it?
p1.a: What I love most is the laid-back lifestyle alongside the welcoming locals. Despite its rapid modernisation, the local community remains exceptionally warm and always ready to lend a helping hand to newcomers.

p1.q: Has your hometown changed much in recent years?
p1.a: Yes, tremendously. In recent years, high-rise hotels and modern infrastructure have sprung up everywhere. While this economic boom has opened up countless career paths, it has also led to heavier traffic congestion during peak hours.

p3.q: Do you think young people want to stay in their hometowns?
p3.a: In my view, most ambitious youngsters nowadays prefer relocating to major metropolitan hubs rather than staying put. The primary catalyst is the vast array of lucrative employment options and modern educational facilities found in big cities. In contrast, smaller hometowns often lack specialised industries, leaving university graduates with fewer professional prospects. Nonetheless, some do eventually move back after gaining experience, seeking a calmer and more affordable lifestyle.

p3.q: How might tourism change a small town?
p3.a: Tourism brings a mixture of remarkable benefits and pronounced challenges to regional towns. On the positive side, it stimulates the local economy by creating jobs in hospitality and retail, often prompting local authorities to upgrade transport infrastructure. However, uncontrolled influxes of visitors frequently result in environmental degradation, inflated living costs, and the commercialisation of indigenous culture, which can gradually erode the town's unique local character.

mistakesVi: Lạm dụng từ 'peaceful' hoặc 'beautiful': Người học thường liên tục lặp lại các tính từ đơn giản này mà không sử dụng các từ vựng Band 7+ phong phú hơn như 'tranquil', 'serene', hay 'picturesque'.

Dùng sai thì khi mô tả sự biến đổi: Khi trả lời câu hỏi về sự thay đổi của quê hương, thí sinh hay dùng thì Quá khứ đơn thay vì thì Hiện tại hoàn thành (Present Perfect) để mô tả quá trình chuyển đổi kéo dài từ quá khứ đến nay.

Nhầm lẫn giữa 'hometown' và 'country': Nhiều bạn nhầm lẫn khi miêu tả quê hương bằng các dữ kiện của cả quốc gia (như diện tích Việt Nam, 54 dân tộc), trong khi 'hometown' chỉ giới hạn ở một thành phố, thị xã hoặc làng quê cụ thể.

housing.sample: If I could choose my dream home, it would be a contemporary two-storey villa nestled on the outskirts of Da Lat. This property would be tucked away in a tranquil residential area surrounded by pine trees, striking a balance between seclusion and convenience. Architecturally, it would embrace minimalist Scandinavian aesthetics, featuring floor-to-ceiling glass windows that flood the spacious interior with natural light and offer panoramic mountain views. Inside, the house would be fully equipped with all the mod cons, including an open-plan kitchen and a solar-powered heating system to keep the space cosy during chilly evenings. Outside, there would be a manicured backyard where I could cultivate herbs and sip my morning coffee. The main reason I would love to live there is the sense of serenity it provides. Life in metropolitan cities is becoming increasingly frantic, so having a peaceful retreat to unwind after demanding workdays would do wonders for my mental well-being. It wouldn’t just be a house; it would be a personal sanctuary where I could truly recharge.

p1.q: Do you live in a house or an apartment?
p1.a: Currently, I live in a modest high-rise apartment on the tenth floor. It’s quite compact, but it suits my lifestyle because it's within walking distance of my workplace and various grocery stores.

p1.q: What is your favourite room in your home?
p1.a: Undoubtedly my bedroom, because it’s my private sanctuary. I’ve decorated it with ambient lighting and indoor plants, so it’s the ideal spot to unwind with a good book after a long, hectic day.

p1.q: Would you like to move to a different home in the future?
p1.a: Yes, definitely. While my current flat is convenient, I hope to relocate to a standalone house with a small garden someday, primarily so my family can enjoy more privacy and fresh outdoor air.

p3.q: What are the main differences between living in a city apartment and living in a countryside house?
p3.a: In my view, the primary distinction lies in the trade-off between convenience and living space. City apartments offer immediate access to modern amenities, public transport, and commercial hubs, though residents often have to endure cramped conditions. Conversely, countryside houses provide generous living spaces and a serene environment, but everyday commuting and accessing specialized healthcare can be considerably more troublesome. Ultimately, it boils down to individual lifestyle priorities.

p3.q: How might housing designs change over the next few decades due to environmental challenges?
p3.a: I believe sustainable architecture will become the norm rather than a luxury. Faced with climate change and escalating energy costs, future dwellings are likely to integrate self-sufficient features such as solar-panel roofs, rainwater harvesting systems, and recycled insulation materials. In contrast to today’s carbon-heavy concrete blocks, upcoming houses will prioritize energy efficiency and climate resilience, helping urban populations reduce their ecological footprint substantially.

mistakesVi: Lạm dụng từ 'convenient' một cách chung chung: Thay vì chỉ lặp đi lặp lại 'My house is very convenient', hãy sử dụng các cụm diễn đạt tự nhiên hơn như 'well-connected', 'within walking distance of...', hoặc 'equipped with all the mod cons'.

Nhầm lẫn giữa 'house' và 'home': 'House' chỉ công trình vật chất cụ thể, trong khi 'home' mang sắc thái tổ ấm và chốn nương tựa cảm xúc; hạn chế nói 'I go to my house to rest' thay vì 'I go home to rest'.

Thiếu mạo từ hoặc sai giới từ khi mô tả nơi chốn: Người học thường quên mạo từ khi nói 'live in apartment' (phải là 'an apartment') hoặc dùng sai giới từ như 'on the city' thay vì 'in the city center' hay 'in a suburban area'.

Ý 1: Mô tả các tính năng cốt lõi (ghi chú, lập kế hoạch, tạo cơ sở dữ liệu tùy biến theo nhu cầu).

internet.sample: I'd like to talk about Notion, an all-in-one productivity workspace that I rely on almost every single day. I initially stumbled upon it two years ago through a tech review on YouTube when I was struggling to organize my university assignments. Essentially, it's a cloud-based platform that combines note-taking, project management, and task tracking into a single customizable dashboard. What makes it stand out is its modular design—you can create databases, embed multimedia, and customize personal planners effortlessly. I usually log in first thing in the morning to review my to-do list and update project deadlines. The main reason I find Notion so indispensable is that it has completely transformed my workflow. Before using it, my study notes were scattered across various notebooks and apps, which caused a lot of mental clutter. Notion has streamlined everything into a centralized hub, saving me hours of searching for information. It basically acts as my second brain, keeping me organized and significantly reducing stress during busy work weeks.

p1.q: How much time do you spend online every day?
p1.a: On average, I'd say around six to seven hours daily. Most of that time is dedicated to work tasks and studying, though I also spend an hour or two unwinding by streaming music or chatting with friends.

p1.q: What do you usually use the internet for?
p1.a: Primarily, I use it for research and daily communication. For instance, I look up academic materials on search engines and rely on messaging apps to coordinate group projects with my classmates throughout the day.

p1.q: Do you think you could live without an internet connection for a week?
p1.a: Honestly, it would be quite tough because my work depends heavily on digital communication. However, if I were on a nature retreat, unplugging for a week might actually be a refreshing and peaceful experience.

p3.q: How has internet access changed the way people acquire knowledge compared to the past?
p3.a: In my view, the internet has fundamentally democratized learning. In the past, people had to visit physical libraries and comb through heavy encyclopedias to find specific information. Nowadays, anyone with a smartphone can access vast databases, online courses, and video tutorials within seconds. While this instant availability fosters self-directed learning, it also requires individuals to filter out misinformation, which was far less prevalent with traditional print media.

p3.q: What are the main risks associated with children having unrestricted access to the web?
p3.a: The most concerning hazard is exposure to inappropriate content, such as violent imagery or online scams, since youngsters often lack critical digital literacy. Moreover, excessive screen time can lead to digital addiction and disrupt sleep patterns, negatively affecting their physical health and social development. Therefore, without parental supervision and safety filters, children remain particularly vulnerable to cyberbullying and exploitation in the virtual world.

Dùng sai giới từ chỉ không gian mạng, phổ biến nhất là nói 'in the internet' thay vì 'on the internet' hoặc dùng trạng từ 'online'.
Lạm dụng từ 'convenience' và 'convenient' để trả lời cho mọi câu hỏi, thiếu những cách diễn đạt học thuật cụ thể như 'enhance efficiency', 'remote accessibility' hay 'facilitate collaboration'.

job-interviews.sample:
I would like to talk about a memorable job interview I had about two years ago when applying for a junior marketing position at a fast-growing tech startup. The interview took place in a glass-walled conference room with two interviewers: the creative director and the head of HR. Both were surprisingly approachable, which helped ease my initial tension.

What made the session unforgettable was an unexpected challenge. Instead of standard questions about strengths and weaknesses, the director handed me a sudden crisis scenario: their flagship app had just received widespread negative reviews, and I had ten minutes to outline a damage-control campaign. I had to think on my feet, quickly structuring a three-step response focusing on transparent communication and user compensation. I fielded their follow-up questions as calmly as possible.

This experience remains vivid because it pushed me out of my comfort zone. Even though it was nerve-racking, I managed to showcase my analytical thinking under pressure rather than rehearsed answers. Ultimately, I landed the job, and that interview taught me that authenticity and problem-solving skills matter far more than flawless memorization.

p1.q: Have you ever attended a job interview?
p1.a: Yes, I have had a couple so far. My most recent one was for a part-time teaching role, where I had to deliver a mock lesson. It was quite demanding, but I passed successfully.

p1.q: How do people usually prepare for an interview in your country?
p1.a: Most applicants thoroughly research the company and rehearse common questions. Many young graduates also practice mock interviews with friends to polish their body language and refine their CVs before the big day.

p1.q: Do you think wearing formal clothes to an interview is still necessary?
p1.a: Generally, yes, because dressing smartly shows respect and professionalism. Even for casual creative firms, opting for neat business attire creates a positive first impression, though strict suits are becoming less mandatory.

p3.q: How have recruitment methods changed over the past decade?
p3.a: In the past, hiring relied heavily on printed resumes and rigid face-to-face panels. Nowadays, digital platforms like LinkedIn and automated video assessments dominate the screening phase. This shift allows employers to evaluate candidate portfolios globally, saving significant time. However, it can sometimes feel impersonal compared to traditional interactions, making cultural evaluation slightly more challenging.

p3.q: Do you think artificial intelligence will completely replace human recruiters in the future?
p3.a: I highly doubt AI will entirely take over. While machine learning algorithms excel at parsing resumes and filtering qualifications efficiently, human intuition remains irreplaceable. Deciding whether an applicant aligns with workplace culture or possesses genuine empathy requires emotional intelligence that machines simply lack. Therefore, AI will likely remain a supportive screening tool rather than a final decision-maker.

mistakesVi: Lạm dụng danh từ 'interview' liên tục thay vì linh hoạt chuyển đổi sang các cụm từ tương đương như 'screening session', 'hiring process', hoặc 'selection round'.
Nhầm lẫn giữa 'interviewer' (người phỏng vấn/nhà tuyển dụng) và 'interviewee' (ứng viên đi phỏng vấn).
Lỗi dùng giới từ sai do ảnh hưởng tiếng Việt: nói 'apply a job' thay vì 'apply for a job', hoặc dịch word-by-word 'pass the interview easily' thiếu tự nhiên.

outlineVi: Mở đầu: Giới thiệu trực tiếp công việc mơ ước (ví dụ: Chuyên gia tư vấn phát triển bền vững cho doanh nghiệp - Sustainable Business Consultant).
Ý 1: Nêu những yêu cầu chuyên môn và kỹ năng cần có như am hiểu kinh tế tuần hoàn, tư duy phân tích dữ liệu và khả năng thuyết phục khách hàng.
Ý 2: Miêu tả các nhiệm vụ chính như khảo sát quy trình phát thải của doanh nghiệp, tư vấn chiến lược chuyển đổi xanh và tổ chức tập huấn nhân sự.
Kết: Nêu lý do đây là công việc lý tưởng vì vừa mang lại thu nhập tốt và sự thăng tiến lâu dài, vừa tạo ra tác động tích cực đối với môi trường xã hội.
jobs.sample: If I could pursue any profession in the foreseeable future, I would love to work as a sustainable business consultant. This role entails advising enterprises on how to reduce their ecological footprint while maintaining commercial profitability. To excel in this field, one needs a solid background in environmental science, coupled with sharp analytical skills and a firm grasp of corporate finance. Furthermore, effective negotiation and interpersonal skills are essential to persuade corporate executives to adopt eco-friendly practices. In this position, my daily responsibilities would involve assessing a company's carbon emissions, auditing their supply chains, and formulating pragmatic sustainability strategies. I would also conduct workshops to foster environmental awareness among employees. I consider this my ideal career because it combines intellectual stimulation with meaningful social impact. Rather than merely chasing a lucrative salary, I aspire to make a tangible contribution toward combating climate change. Additionally, the green economy is rapidly expanding, offering robust job security alongside vast potential for career advancement.

p1.q: Do you currently work or are you a student?
p1.a: I am currently working full-time as a digital marketer for a retail firm. My day-to-day work mainly involves managing social media campaigns and analyzing customer metrics, which I find quite dynamic and engaging.

p1.q: What do you enjoy most about your daily work routine?
p1.a: What I appreciate most is the creative autonomy my manager grants me. For instance, when designing new advertising campaigns, I am free to experiment with novel visual concepts, which keeps my job exciting and fulfilling.

p1.q: Would you like to change your job or career path in the future?
p1.a: Yes, I would certainly like to transition into data analytics eventually. Although marketing is enjoyable, data science offers higher job security and lucrative remuneration, especially with the exponential rise of tech-driven businesses in Vietnam.

p3.q: How do you think artificial intelligence will change the nature of employment in the coming decades?
p3.a: I believe artificial intelligence will primarily automate routine, administrative tasks, shifting human labor toward higher-order creative and strategic responsibilities. For instance, while data entry clerks might become obsolete, demand for prompt engineers and ethical AI overseers will surge. Consequently, workers will need continuous reskilling to stay competitive, as adaptability will become the single most vital asset in the automated workforce.

p3.q: Should governments prioritize job security or labor market flexibility when formulating economic policies?
p3.a: In my view, governments must strike a delicate balance between both priorities rather than favoring one exclusively. Overly rigid job protections can discourage foreign investment and hinder innovation, whereas extreme flexibility often leaves workers vulnerable to exploitation and sudden unemployment. A viable solution is the Nordic flexicurity model, which combines easy hiring and firing with robust social safety nets and state-funded retraining programs.

mistakesVi: Nhầm lẫn giữa 'work', 'job' và 'career': Thí sinh thường dùng sai ngữ pháp như nói 'a work' thay vì 'a job' (vì 'work' là danh từ không đếm được khi chỉ công việc nói chung), hoặc dùng 'career' khi chỉ một vị trí làm việc cụ thể.

Dịch từng từ từ tiếng Việt (word-by-word translation): Dùng các cụm thiếu tự nhiên như 'make high salary' thay vì 'earn a competitive salary', hoặc 'have a lot of work' thay vì 'handle a heavy workload'.

Lặp từ vựng cơ bản và thiếu tính học thuật: Quá lạm dụng các từ đơn giản như 'hard', 'busy', 'money' thay vì diễn đạt tự nhiên ở Band 7+ với các cụm như 'demanding', 'lucrative income', 'work-life balance' hay 'career prospects'.

outlineVi: Mở đầu: Giới thiệu ngôn ngữ bạn ấp ủ muốn học (ví dụ: tiếng Nhật) và bối cảnh bạn bắt đầu say mê nó.
Ý 1: Kế hoạch học tập cụ thể (kết hợp tự học qua ứng dụng số và luyện giao tiếp định kỳ với người bản xứ).
Ý 2: Những rào cản bạn lường trước (hệ thống chữ viết phức tạp như Kanji, các cấp độ kính ngữ trong giao tiếp).
Kết: Lý do muốn chinh phục ngôn ngữ này (du lịch tự túc, thưởng thức văn hóa nguyên bản và mở rộng sự nghiệp).
language-learning.sample: If I had the opportunity to pick up another foreign language, I would definitely choose Japanese. I've always been fascinated by Japanese culture, from its traditional arts to modern anime and gaming. To master it, my plan is to adopt a blended learning approach. Initially, I'd rely on language apps and podcasts to grasp the fundamentals of vocabulary and basic grammar. Afterwards, I would hire a native tutor online for weekly conversational practice to sharpen my speaking fluency. Of course, I know it won't be a walk in the park. The biggest hurdle will likely be mastering the complex writing systems, especially Kanji characters, which require immense memorization. Besides, Japanese honorifics and polite speech levels can be quite tricky for beginners. Nevertheless, I am keen on learning it because I want to travel across Japan without relying on translation apps, and perhaps even collaborate with Japanese partners in my future career. Experiencing a culture through its own tongue would be immensely rewarding.

p1.q: How many languages can you speak?
p1.a: Aside from my mother tongue, Vietnamese, I can speak English fluently. I use it every day for study and work, and I've also picked up a few basic Korean phrases from watching dramas.

p1.q: What do you find most challenging about learning a new language?
p1.a: I'd say mastering natural pronunciation and colloquial expressions is the hardest part. You can easily memorize grammar rules from textbooks, but sounding natural in everyday dialogue requires constant exposure and practice.

p1.q: Do you prefer learning a language independently or in a classroom?
p1.a: I prefer self-study because it allows me to progress at my own pace. Using podcasts and digital flashcards suits my schedule better than rigid classroom sessions, although classes are great for practicing speaking.

p3.q: Do you think artificial intelligence and translation tools will make language learning obsolete?
p3.a: I don't think automated tools will ever completely replace language learning. While AI can instantly translate texts and speech with impressive accuracy, it often misses cultural nuances, humor, and emotional depth. Furthermore, learning a language isn't just about exchanging practical information; it's about forming genuine human connections. Therefore, people will still want to speak foreign languages to build empathy and immerse themselves in different cultures.

p3.q: Why do children often pick up foreign languages more quickly than adults?
p3.a: In my view, children benefit from brain plasticity and an instinctive way of acquiring language through play and social interaction. Unlike adults, they are generally less self-conscious about making mistakes or mispronouncing words. In contrast, adults often overanalyze grammatical structures and feel anxious about sounding silly, which slows down their progress. Hence, an uninhibited mindset gives young learners a distinct advantage.

mistakesVi: Lặp lại từ 'language' quá nhiều lần thay vì dùng các từ thay thế tự nhiên như 'mother tongue', 'target language', 'second language' hoặc dùng đại từ.
Dùng cách diễn đạt gượng gạo do dịch trực tiếp từ tiếng Việt, chẳng hạn nói 'talk English' thay vì 'speak English', hoặc 'know a language' thay vì 'achieve fluency in a language'.
Trả lời quá ngắn và chỉ nêu lợi ích sáo rỗng (như 'to get a good job') mà quên bàn sâu về khía cạnh ngôn ngữ như ngữ pháp, phát âm hay sự thấu cảm văn hóa.

outlineVi: Mở đầu: Giới thiệu người bạn muốn kể (ví dụ: cựu nhóm trưởng Minh trong chiến dịch gây quỹ năm cuối đại học).
Ý 1 (Bối cảnh): Nêu thời gian và áp lực cực lớn khi nhóm chỉ có ba tuần để tổ chức sự kiện và gặp sự cố mất địa điểm.
Ý 2 (Hành động): Kể cách người đó giữ bình tĩnh, phân chia việc theo thế mạnh từng người, cùng thức đêm làm banner và giải quyết xung đột.
Kết: Nhấn mạnh lý do lãnh đạo hiệu quả là vì họ biết truyền cảm hứng, lắng nghe và trao quyền thay vì áp đặt quyền lực.
leadership.sample:
I would like to talk about Minh, who was my team leader during our final-year university charity campaign. We were tasked with organizing an art auction within just three weeks, and the emotional pressure on our squad was immense.

Minh stood out immediately due to his calm demeanor. Instead of panicking or micromanaging, he gathered everyone to brainstorm, carefully assessed each member's strengths, and delegated tasks accordingly. When our reserved venue backed out at the last minute, causing widespread panic, he took decisive action. He remained composed, rallied the troops, and negotiated an alternative sponsorship deal within twenty-four hours.

What made his leadership truly exceptional was his ability to lead by example. He did not simply sit back and issue instructions; he stayed up late alongside us assembling promotional materials. Furthermore, his conflict resolution skills kept the group unified despite severe exhaustion.

Ultimately, the exhibition raised substantial funds for local orphanages. I deeply admire Minh because he proved that authentic leadership is not about exerting dominance, but about empowering others and staying grounded under immense strain.

p1.q: Have you ever been the leader of a team or a project?
p1.a: Yes, I led a student committee back at university. We organized cultural workshops and charity drives. Although managing logistical headaches was challenging, it taught me how to coordinate people and make quick decisions under pressure.

p1.q: Do you prefer working independently or leading a group?
p1.a: To be honest, it depends on the task. For deep analytical assignments, I prefer working solo to concentrate fully, whereas for creative campaigns, leading a group is far more rewarding because collective brainstorming yields better results.

p1.q: What kind of qualities do you think make a good school monitor or team captain?
p1.a: I believe empathy and active listening are paramount. A decent captain needs to treat everyone equitably and communicate transparently, ensuring that every teammate feels valued and genuinely motivated to pull their weight together.

p3.q: Do you think great leaders are born with their abilities, or can leadership be taught?
p3.a: In my view, while some individuals naturally possess charismatic personalities, leadership is largely a skill refined through experience. People can learn communication strategies, emotional resilience, and conflict management through deliberate mentorship and practical exposure. Many introverted professionals evolve into remarkable executives after formal managerial training, demonstrating that nurture plays a far more decisive role than innate talent.

p3.q: How has the definition of a good leader changed compared to past generations?
p3.a: Historically, leadership was equated with autocratic authority, where strict hierarchy and unquestioned obedience prevailed. Nowadays, contemporary workplaces prioritize empathetic leadership, emotional intelligence, and shared governance. Modern leaders act primarily as facilitators who foster psychological safety and invite input, contrasting sharply with the traditional command-and-control paradigm of previous eras.

mistakesVi: Lạm dụng từ 'leader' và 'lead' lặp lại quá nhiều lần thay vì biến hóa bằng các cụm như 'take the helm', 'head up a team', hay 'provide guidance'.
Dùng sai giới từ hoặc cấu trúc, ví dụ dịch máy 'lead someone to do something' trong ngữ cảnh quản lý nhóm thay vì dùng 'guide the team' hoặc 'oversee members'.
Trả lời Part 3 quá thiên về cảm tính cá nhân (chỉ khen ngợi tính tốt bụng, hiền lành) mà quên bàn luận về khía cạnh quản trị, trách nhiệm giải trình và văn hóa tổ chức.

outlineVi: Mở đầu: Giới thiệu tên và vị trí của thư viện (Thư viện Quốc gia Việt Nam ở trung tâm Hà Nội).
Ý 1: Mô tả cơ sở vật chất, kiến trúc Pháp cổ điển kết hợp thiết bị hiện đại và nguồn học liệu đa dạng.
Ý 2: Thuật lại hoạt động cụ thể (tìm tài liệu nghiên cứu khóa luận tốt nghiệp, ngồi tự học tại phòng đọc yên tĩnh).
Kết: Giải thích ấn tượng sâu sắc (bầu không khí học thuật tĩnh lặng truyền cảm hứng và sự đối lập kỳ diệu với phố xá ồn ào bên ngoài).
libraries.sample:
I’d like to talk about the National Library of Vietnam, nestled right in the heart of Hanoi on Trang Thi Street. It is an extraordinary space that seamlessly blends French colonial architecture with state-of-the-art facilities.

The library boasts a massive collection spanning rare historical manuscripts, academic periodicals, and an extensive digital database. There are also spacious, naturally lit reading rooms, private multimedia booths, and a leafy courtyard outside.

I visited it a couple of years ago while working on my undergraduate dissertation. Desperate for a distraction-free environment, I tucked myself away in an air-conditioned reading hall on the second floor. I spent hours sifting through physical archives and accessing peer-reviewed journals on their terminals.

What impressed me most was the serene, almost reverent atmosphere. Despite being located in a bustling urban district, the interior was totally insulated from traffic noise, making it remarkably conducive to deep focus. Seeing people of all ages—from elderly researchers to high school students—absorbed in their reading really inspired me and revitalized my love for quiet scholarship.

p1.q: How often do you visit libraries?
p1.a: To be honest, I rarely visit physical libraries these days, maybe once every few months. I conduct most of my reading digitally on tablets, although I still drop by my local university library when I urgently need a quiet, distraction-free corner.

p1.q: Did you go to a library when you were a child?
p1.a: Yes, definitely. My primary school had a modest reading room, and I used to spend my lunch breaks there. I was particularly fascinated by illustrated fairy tales and science encyclopedias, which sparked my lifelong curiosity.

p1.q: Do you prefer studying in a library or at home?
p1.a: I definitely lean towards libraries because the disciplined ambiance helps me stay focused. At home, there are simply too many temptations, like household chores or social media, whereas a library peer-pressures me into productive study sessions.

p3.q: In what ways have digital resources altered the traditional role of libraries?
p3.a: Digital platforms have shifted libraries from mere warehouses of printed books into versatile community learning hubs. Instead of simply borrowing physical paperbacks, patrons nowadays utilize online repositories, high-speed internet, and collaborative co-working desks. That said, the physical space remains indispensable for those without reliable digital access at home. Ultimately, modern libraries have evolved to complement digital connectivity rather than being replaced by it.

p3.q: Should governments continue to allocate public funds to maintain physical libraries?
p3.a: I firmly believe public investment in libraries should continue. While some consider them costly relics, public libraries ensure equitable access to educational resources for underprivileged demographics who cannot afford personal computers or premium subscriptions. Furthermore, they serve as vital social venues that foster community cohesion. Cutting public funding would inevitably deepen the educational divide between socioeconomic classes.

mistakesVi: Dùng lẫn lộn giữa 'library' (thư viện - nơi mượn đọc miễn phí) và 'bookstore' (nhà sách - nơi mua bán), ví dụ nói nhầm 'I bought three books at the library'.
Lạm dụng lặp đi lặp lại cụm từ đơn giản 'quiet and peaceful' thay vì dùng các tính từ học thuật phong phú như 'conducive to learning', 'distraction-free', hay 'studious environment'.
Phát âm sai từ 'library' do nuốt âm /r/ hoặc đọc thành /ˈlaɪbəri/ thay vì hai cách chuẩn: /ˈlaɪbrəri/ (Anh-Anh) hoặc /ˈlaɪbreri/ (Anh-Mỹ).

outlineVi: Mở đầu: Giới thiệu sự kiện tuổi thơ đáng nhớ nhất (lần đi lạc tại hội chợ hoa Tết năm 7 tuổi).
Ý 1: Mô tả bối cảnh thời gian, địa điểm đông đúc và người đi cùng (mẹ và chị gái).
Ý 2: Kể lại chi tiết diễn biến (bị cuốn hút bởi gian hàng tò he, lạc mất người thân, cảm giác hoảng loạn và được người bán hàng tốt bụng giúp đỡ).
Kết: Giải thích lý do sự kiện in sâu vào tâm trí (bài học đầu đời về sự cẩn thận và lòng biết ơn đối với sự tử tế của người lạ).
memory.sample:
One childhood memory that is still etched in my mind happened when I was around seven years old during the Lunar New Year festival. My mother and older sister took me to a bustling floral market in our hometown to pick up peach blossoms.

Surrounded by vibrant blooms and massive crowds, I got completely mesmerized by a stall selling colourful traditional dough figurines. When I turned around, my family had vanished in the sea of shoppers. A wave of sheer panic washed over me, and I started sobbing uncontrollably. Fortunately, an elderly vendor noticed my distress. She offered me a warm sweet treat to calm me down and immediately contacted the market security. Within twenty minutes, my frantic mother rushed into the booth, hugging me with tears of relief.

I still recall this incident so vividly because it was my first real brush with vulnerability. More importantly, it taught me a lifelong lesson about attentiveness and showed me how profound the kindness of strangers can be, leaving an indelible imprint on who I am today.

p1.q: Do you have a good memory for numbers or names?
p1.a: Honestly, I'm much better with names than numbers. When I meet someone, their face and name usually stick with me, whereas I constantly struggle to memorize bank details or phone numbers without writing them down.

p1.q: How do you usually remind yourself of important tasks?
p1.a: I rely heavily on digital productivity tools. I set calendar alerts on my smartphone for deadlines and keep a sticky note widget on my desktop for daily errands, ensuring nothing slips through the cracks.

p1.q: Have you ever forgotten something really important?
p1.a: Yes, once I completely forgot my passport before heading to the airport for an overseas flight. I had to pay an exorbitant taxi fare to rush back home, which was an absolute nightmare.

p3.q: Why do people tend to remember negative experiences more vividly than positive ones?
p3.a: I believe this stems from human evolutionary biology. Our ancestors had to remember dangerous threats to survive, which makes distressing events deeply imprinted in our psyche. For instance, getting burned once teaches a child caution for years. While positive events bring joy, negative ones act as protective mechanisms against future adversity, so our brains prioritize retaining them.

p3.q: How has modern technology influenced human memory and retention skills?
p3.a: Modern technology has undeniably outsourced much of our memory capacity. With smartphones instantly storing contacts, dates, and navigation routes, people rarely exercise their cognitive recall. While this digital convenience frees up mental bandwidth for analytical tasks, it also leads to digital amnesia, where individuals struggle to retain even basic factual information without immediate internet assistance.

mistakesVi: Dùng nhầm giữa 'remember' và 'remind': Thí sinh thường nói 'He remembered me to do this' thay vì 'He reminded me to do this'.
Lạm dụng từ 'memory' một cách gượng gạo thay vì dùng tính từ hoặc cụm động từ tự nhiên (ví dụ nói 'I have bad memory of it' thay vì 'My memory of it is rather hazy').
Chỉ sử dụng duy nhất thì quá khứ đơn (Past Simple) suốt cả bài Part 2 mà bỏ qua thì quá khứ hoàn thành (Past Perfect) để diễn tả sự việc xảy ra trước một mốc quá khứ khác.

outlineVi: Mở đầu: Giới thiệu ngắn gọn tên ứng dụng (Notion), mục đích chính (quản lý công việc/ghi chép) và bối cảnh biết đến app (được bạn đại học giới thiệu).
Ý 1 - Tính năng nổi bật: Miêu tả giao diện tối giản, khả năng đồng bộ đa nền tảng tức thì và các bảng kế hoạch tùy biến linh hoạt.
Ý 2 - Tần suất và bối cảnh sử dụng: Mở ứng dụng nhiều lần trong ngày (buổi sáng để lập to-do list, ban ngày để ghi chú bài học, kỳ thi dùng làm trung tâm ôn tập).
Kết - Lý do không thể thiếu: Nhấn mạnh app giúp tổ chức cuộc sống ngăn nắp, giảm căng thẳng quên bài và tối ưu hóa năng suất cá nhân.
mobile-apps.sample: I would like to talk about Notion, an all-in-one productivity app that has become an indispensable part of my day-to-day life. I first stumbled upon it about two years ago through a classmate’s recommendation when we were struggling to organize group assignments. Essentially, Notion functions as a flexible workspace where you can take notes, create databases, and manage to-do lists. What sets it apart is its clean, user-friendly interface and seamless cross-platform syncing, which lets me switch between my phone and laptop without missing a beat. I open this app multiple times a day. Every morning, I check my master planner to prioritize tasks, and throughout the day, I use it to jot down sudden ideas or track my fitness regime. Whenever exams approach, it acts as my primary revision hub. The main reason it is so essential to me is that it has completely transformed my time management. Before adopting Notion, I was constantly overwhelmed by sticky notes and scattered reminders. Now, everything is centralized in one reliable place, saving me hours of stress and keeping my academic life thoroughly on track.

p1.q: What kinds of mobile apps do you use most frequently on your smartphone?
p1.a: I primarily depend on utility and communication tools like Telegram and Google Calendar. These apps help me stay connected with colleagues and structure my daily schedule efficiently without getting distracted by endless social media feeds.

p1.q: Have your preferences for apps changed compared to when you were younger?
p1.a: Definitely. In high school, I spent hours playing mobile games and browsing photo-sharing platforms. Nowadays, however, I gravitate towards productivity and language learning apps such as Duolingo to support my self-improvement goals.

p1.q: Do you think you spend too much time using mobile applications?
p1.a: Honestly, yes, especially on video-streaming platforms. Although I try to set strict screen time limits, I often catch myself scrolling late into the night, which sometimes compromises my sleep quality.

p3.q: How have mobile applications altered the way people communicate in modern society?
p3.a: Mobile apps have made interpersonal communication instantaneous and borderless. Through instant messaging and video-calling platforms, individuals can bridge physical distances and collaborate seamlessly across time zones. Nevertheless, this shift has also replaced nuanced face-to-face dialogues with brief, superficial text exchanges. While our reach has broadened significantly, the emotional depth of interpersonal relationships has somewhat diminished as a result.

p3.q: To what extent do you agree that mobile software may pose significant risks to personal privacy?
p3.a: I strongly believe that modern apps present serious privacy hazards. Many applications routinely harvest sensitive user data, including geographical locations and browsing habits, often selling this information to third-party advertisers without explicit consent. While data collection can personalize user experiences, frequent corporate data breaches demonstrate that unchecked digital tracking leaves consumers exceptionally vulnerable to identity theft and unwanted surveillance.

mistakesVi: Lạm dụng từ 'software' thay cho 'app/application': Trong văn nói tự nhiên khi nhắc đến điện thoại, người bản xứ hầu như dùng 'app', còn 'software' thường dùng cho hệ thống hoặc máy tính để bàn.
Dùng sai giới từ chỉ không gian ứng dụng: Người học hay nói nhầm 'in my phone' hoặc 'in the app', trong khi cấu trúc chuẩn xác phải dùng giới từ 'on' ('on my smartphone', 'on this app').

Thiếu các cụm collocation tự nhiên: Thí sinh thường dùng tính từ đơn lẻ như 'the app is good/easy' thay vì các cụm Band 7+ chuẩn xác như 'user-friendly interface', 'seamless integration', hay 'in-app features'.

outlineVi: Mở đầu: Giới thiệu món đồ đã tiết kiệm để mua (chiếc máy tính xách tay cao cấp phục vụ đồ họa) và lý do cần nó vào thời điểm đó.
Ý 1: Nêu rõ khoảng thời gian tích cóp (khoảng sáu tháng) và nguồn tiền từ công việc dạy kèm thêm.
Ý 2: Miêu tả phương pháp tiết kiệm cụ thể (thắt chặt chi tiêu, tự nấu ăn ở nhà, dùng ứng dụng theo dõi ngân sách cá nhân).
Kết: Bày tỏ niềm tự hào khi thanh toán bằng tiền tự tay làm ra và giá trị lâu dài mà thiết bị mang lại cho công việc.
money.sample: I would like to talk about a time when I saved up money to purchase a high-end laptop, specifically a MacBook Air, which I desperately needed for my university coursework and freelance design gigs. This happened roughly two years ago when my old computer abruptly gave up the ghost. The machine cost around one thousand dollars, which was a formidable sum for a student like me. It took me approximately six months of disciplined budgeting to amass that amount. To achieve this goal, I had to tighten my belt considerably. I took on extra evening tutoring shifts and made a conscious effort to prepare meals at home rather than eating out with friends. Every spare penny went straight into a dedicated savings fund so that I wouldn't be tempted to splurge. When I finally walked into the retail store and paid in full with my own hard-earned money, I felt an immense sense of pride. It wasn't merely a reliable work tool, but tangible proof that I could achieve a tough financial target through self-restraint.

p1.q: Do you prefer paying with cash or using digital payment methods?
p1.a: I definitely lean towards cashless options like mobile banking and digital wallets. They are incredibly convenient and save me from carrying bulky change, plus they automatically record my transactions, which makes budgeting effortless.

p1.q: Did you save money when you were a child?
p1.a: Yes, I did. My parents gifted me a ceramic piggy bank where I regularly stored lucky money from New Year celebrations and spare change, which I later spent on storybooks.

p1.q: What kind of things do you usually spend most of your money on?
p1.a: The lion's share of my monthly budget goes towards essentials like groceries and public transit. Occasionally, I allocate some funds for online learning courses to develop my professional skill set.

p3.q: Why do some people find it difficult to manage their personal finances effectively?
p3.a: In my view, impulsive consumerism driven by targeted advertising and peer pressure is the main culprit. Many individuals live beyond their means just to project an affluent lifestyle on social media. Moreover, a widespread lack of budgeting education leaves people unable to plan for unforeseen expenses, eventually trapping them in vicious cycles of consumer debt.

p3.q: To what extent should financial literacy be taught as a compulsory subject in schools?
p3.a: I strongly believe that personal finance should be mandatory in the secondary school curriculum. While abstract subjects like calculus have merit, understanding taxation, compound interest, and debt management directly impacts every adult's quality of life. Teaching youngsters these practical competencies early produces responsible consumers and builds a far more financially resilient society overall.

mistakesVi: Dùng sai cấu trúc với động từ chỉ chi phí: người học hay nói 'I cost 50 dollars for this shirt' thay vì cấu trúc đúng là 'This shirt cost me 50 dollars' hoặc 'I spent 50 dollars on this shirt'.
Lạm dụng danh từ 'money' ở dạng số nhiều không chuẩn ('moneys') hoặc đi với lượng từ sai như 'many money' thay vì dùng 'a large amount of money' hay 'a lot of money'.

Thiếu các cách diễn đạt Band 7+ về tiền tệ, dẫn đến việc lặp đi lặp lại những từ cơ bản như 'cheap', 'expensive', 'buy' thay vì các cụm tự nhiên như 'budget-friendly', 'exorbitant', hoặc 'live within one's means'.

outlineVi: Mở đầu: Giới thiệu bảo tàng bạn muốn kể (Bảo tàng Dân tộc học Việt Nam ở Hà Nội) và thời điểm ghé thăm gần đây.
Ý 1 (Nơi chốn & Người đồng hành): Nêu vị trí cụ thể ở quận Cầu Giấy và người bạn đi cùng vào dịp cuối tuần.
Ý 2 (Hiện vật trưng bày): Miêu tả trang phục thổ cẩm, nhạc cụ truyền thống và điểm nhấn là khu vườn kiến trúc ngoài trời với nhà rông, nhà dài.
Kết (Lý do ấn tượng): Giải thích trải nghiệm tương tác chân thực và cách bảo tàng tái hiện lịch sử sống động, sâu sắc hơn sách giáo khoa.
museums.sample: I would like to talk about the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology, located in the Cau Giay district of Hanoi. I visited it last autumn with one of my close friends who was in town for the weekend. The museum showcases the diverse cultural heritage of Vietnam's 54 ethnic groups. Inside, there are thousands of everyday objects, elaborate tribal costumes, and traditional musical instruments on display. What really sets it apart, though, is the open-air architectural garden. It features full-scale replicas of traditional dwellings, such as the towering communal house of the Ba Na people and an authentic Ede longhouse. The reason this visit left such a lasting impression on me was how immersive the whole experience felt. Rather than keeping visitors behind velvet ropes, the museum offers a hands-on experience where you can step directly into the thatched houses and listen to audio recordings of traditional folk songs. It truly brought history to life and deepened my appreciation for the cultural richness of our country, making it far more memorable than any standard textbook lesson.

p1.q: Do you often visit museums or art galleries?
p1.a: To be honest, not very often, perhaps once or twice a year. I usually go when there is a special temporary exhibition in town, like the recent lacquer painting showcase at our local fine arts gallery.

p1.q: What kind of museums do you find most interesting?
p1.a: I am particularly drawn to interactive science museums. Rather than just staring at static objects behind glass, I love hands-on exhibits where you can press buttons, run small experiments, and see scientific concepts in action.

p1.q: Did you go to any museums when you were a child?
p1.a: Yes, definitely. My elementary school organized annual field trips to the National History Museum. I vividly remember marveling at ancient stone tools and giant replica boats alongside all my classmates.

p3.q: Should public museums charge admission fees or be entirely free for citizens?
p3.a: In my view, public museums should ideally be free or charge only nominal fees. Since these institutions preserve shared cultural heritage, universal access ensures that people from all socio-economic backgrounds can benefit from educational resources. However, while relying on state funding is ideal, charging a small fee for special exhibits can help maintain preservation standards without alienating lower-income visitors. Balancing accessibility with financial sustainability is key.

p3.q: How might virtual museum tours change the way people appreciate cultural heritage in the future?
p3.a: Virtual tours are revolutionizing cultural engagement by democratizing access. Anyone with an internet connection can now explore global collections like the Louvre without paying for costly international flights. Nevertheless, high-resolution screens cannot completely replace the visceral emotional impact of standing in front of a real centuries-old masterpiece. Ultimately, virtual tours will serve as an enticing preview rather than a total substitute for genuine physical visits.

mistakesVi: Lặp từ 'museum' hoặc 'history' liên tục; nên luân chuyển linh hoạt bằng 'exhibition', 'cultural institution', 'gallery', hoặc 'heritage site'.
Dùng sai cụm cố định, ví dụ nói 'in display' thay vì 'on display', hoặc nhầm lẫn giữa 'artifact' (cổ vật nhân tạo) và 'antique' (đồ cổ thông thường).
Phát âm sai trọng âm của từ 'museum' (/mjuːˈziː.əm/), người học Việt Nam thường có xu hướng nhấn vào âm tiết đầu tiên thay vì âm tiết thứ hai.

outlineVi: Mở đầu: Giới thiệu tên bài hát ('Fix You' của ban nhạc rock Coldplay), thể loại và vị trí đặc biệt của nó trong đời sống tinh thần của bạn.
Ý 1 (Khi nghe lần đầu): Kể hoàn cảnh nghe bài hát lần đầu vào giai đoạn ôn thi đại học căng thẳng, qua một chiếc tai nghe được bạn thân chia sẻ.
Ý 2 (Ý nghĩa): Giải thích thông điệp về sự kiên cường và an ủi vô điều kiện, nhắc nhở rằng vấp ngã là điều bình thường và hy vọng luôn ở phía trước.
Kết (Tại sao đặc biệt): Nhấn mạnh bài hát như một điểm tựa cảm xúc (emotional anchor) giúp xoa dịu áp lực và nhắc nhớ về tình bạn đẹp đẽ.
music.sample: I'd like to talk about 'Fix You' by the British rock band Coldplay, a song that holds a genuinely special place in my heart. I first stumbled upon it about five years ago during high school. It was an extremely stressful period because I was preparing for the grueling university entrance exams. One late afternoon in the school library, feeling thoroughly burnt out, my best friend handed me an earbud and pressed play. From the opening church organ chords to Chris Martin's gentle vocals, the track instantly struck a chord with me. The lyrics convey a message of unconditional support and resilience, reminding the listener that it's okay to falter and that hope will always guide you through dark times. What makes this song truly unique to me is that it acts as an emotional anchor. Whenever I experience setbacks at work or in my personal life, playing 'Fix You' helps me mellow out and puts things into perspective. More than just a piece of music, it serves as a comforting reminder of my friend's kindness and my own capacity to overcome hardships.

p1.q: What kind of music do you like?
p1.a: I have quite an eclectic taste, but I mostly lean towards indie pop and R&B. Upbeat melodies really lift my spirits, so I frequently listen to artists like Lauv or Daniel Caesar during my daily commute.

p1.q: Do you play any musical instruments?
p1.a: Honestly, I don't play any instruments because I'm virtually tone-deaf. I attempted to pick up the acoustic guitar a few years ago, but my clumsy fingers just couldn't master the chords, so I gave up.

p1.q: Do you listen to music when you study?
p1.a: Yes, but strictly instrumental tunes or lo-fi beats without lyrics. Songs with words tend to distract me, whereas ambient background music helps drown out surrounding noise and keeps me focused on challenging tasks.

p3.q: Why do people like different kinds of music?
p3.a: I believe musical preference is largely shaped by personality and cultural upbringing. For instance, energetic individuals often gravitate towards EDM or rock for stimulation, while introverted people might prefer classical or acoustic pieces to unwind. Additionally, the music we are exposed to during our teenage years creates deep emotional attachments. Therefore, diversity in personal experiences naturally leads to varied musical tastes.

p3.q: Should music be taught in all schools?
p3.a: Undoubtedly, yes. Music education fosters creativity and stimulates cognitive development in ways that traditional academic subjects cannot. For example, learning to read sheet music enhances spatial-temporal reasoning and mathematical thinking. Some argue that schools should focus exclusively on STEM subjects, but neglecting arts like music deprives children of a vital emotional outlet. Hence, it should definitely remain an integral part of the core curriculum.

mistakesVi: Dùng sai ngữ pháp với danh từ không đếm được: 'Music' là uncountable noun, người học thường quen miệng nói 'a music' hoặc 'many musics' thay vì 'a piece of music', 'a genre of music' hoặc dùng từ 'songs'.
Thiếu giới từ hoặc mạo từ: Rất nhiều thí sinh nói 'I often listen music' (thiếu 'to') hoặc 'I can play guitar' thay vì cụm chuẩn 'play the guitar' (nhạc cụ sau động từ play luôn cần mạo từ 'the').

Lạm dụng cách dịch thô từ tiếng Việt: Thường lặp đi lặp lại cụm 'relax my brain' hay 'relax my mind' (nghe gượng gạo trong tiếng Anh) thay vì dùng các cách diễn đạt tự nhiên như 'unwind', 'mellow out' hoặc 'take my mind off work'.

nature.sample: I'd like to share my experience visiting Ba Vi National Park, a stunning mountainous sanctuary nestled just outside Hanoi. I traveled there last autumn with a couple of close friends to take a weekend break from university life. The landscape was genuinely breathtaking, surrounded by mist-shrouded peaks and dense, lush greenery. As soon as we arrived, the cool, crisp mountain breeze felt like an instant breath of fresh air. We spent the morning trekking along winding stone trails, marveling at the rich flora and fauna and visiting an old French colonial church wrapped in moss. In the afternoon, we pitched a small tent near a pine forest and had a picnic while basking in the gentle sunlight. This trip made an indelible impression on me primarily because of the tranquil atmosphere. Living in a noisy concrete jungle, I constantly battle traffic and screen fatigue. Being able to commune with nature in such a serene environment completely recharged my mental batteries. It reminded me how vital untouched green spaces are for our emotional well-being.

p1.q: Do you often visit parks or botanical gardens?
p1.a: Yes, definitely. I make a habit of strolling through a nearby park every weekend morning to get some fresh air. It provides a peaceful retreat where I can stretch my legs and decompress after a hectic week.

p1.q: What do you usually like to do when you are in natural surroundings?
p1.a: I usually prefer brisk walking or simply sitting on a bench listening to natural sounds like birds chirping. Immersing myself in scenic landscapes helps clear my mind, especially when I listen to instrumental music on my headphones.

p1.q: Did you spend much time outdoors when you were a child?
p1.a: Yes, absolutely. Growing up in the countryside, I spent almost every afternoon playing football in open fields with neighborhood kids. We used to climb fruit trees and explore small streams, which kept us active and connected with nature.

p3.q: Why is it important for cities to incorporate public green spaces into urban planning?
p3.a: I believe urban green spaces are indispensable for both public health and environmental balance. Dense cities frequently suffer from severe air pollution and the urban heat island effect, which lush parks can actively mitigate by absorbing carbon dioxide. Moreover, these spaces offer residents essential recreational areas to exercise and socialize, significantly reducing stress levels compared to overcrowded indoor shopping malls. Therefore, green urban planning fosters healthier communities.

p3.q: How might modern technology affect younger generations' connection with the natural world?
p3.a: Undoubtedly, pervasive technology has created a widening gap between young people and the outdoors. Sedentary indoor habits, driven by video games and social media, often discourage teenagers from exploring natural parks. However, if used thoughtfully, digital tools like wildlife identification apps or nature vlogs can spark genuine curiosity about biodiversity. Ultimately, while screens pose an obvious distraction, they can also serve as educational catalysts if balanced properly.

mistakesVi: Lạm dụng từ 'nature' sai ngữ pháp: Thường dùng nhầm 'nature park' thay vì 'natural park', hoặc quên mất 'nature' là danh từ không đếm được và không đi kèm mạo từ 'the' khi nói về thiên nhiên nói chung.
Lỗi phát âm các từ quen thuộc: Rất nhiều thí sinh phát âm sai trọng âm của từ 'atmosphere' (/ˈætməsfɪər/ nhấn âm 1) hoặc đọc sai nguyên âm của 'fauna' (/ˈfɔːnə/).

Diễn đạt ý quá đơn giản và lặp từ: Thường xuyên lặp lại cụm 'it makes me feel relaxed' thay vì dùng các cụm diễn đạt tự nhiên, giàu hình ảnh hơn như 'unwind', 'recharge my mental batteries' hay 'commune with nature'.

neighbours.sample:
I'd like to talk about Mr. Nam, a retired school principal who lives directly opposite my family's house. I first encountered him about three years ago during a weekend neighbourhood cleanup. While most residents were somewhat hesitant to participate, he took the initiative with great enthusiasm, which immediately left an impression on me.

Over the past few years, Mr. Nam has transformed our street into a truly vibrant and close-knit community. His most notable initiative was turning a neglected patch of vacant land at the corner of our alley into a flourishing communal herb garden. Besides that, he coordinated a weekly recycling program and routinely checks on elderly residents who live on their own.

I believe his efforts have made an extraordinary difference because he managed to break the ice among neighbours who previously barely exchanged greetings. Living in a bustling city often isolates people, yet his selflessness rekindled our shared civic spirit. Thanks to him, our neighbourhood feels noticeably safer, warmer, and far more connected than it ever was before.

p1.q: How well do you know the people who live next door to you?
p1.a: I know them quite well because we have lived on the same floor for five years. We often exchange homemade dishes during traditional holidays and occasionally stop for a friendly chat in the hallway.

p1.q: How often do you interact with your neighbours?
p1.a: I bump into them almost every day while waiting for the elevator or collecting parcels. On weekends, we sometimes grab morning coffee together at the local cafe just around the corner.

p1.q: Do you think it is important to have a good relationship with your neighbours?
p1.a: Definitely, because neighbours are the closest support network in times of emergency. For instance, when my pipes burst last winter, my adjacent neighbour immediately lent me tools and helped shut off the main valve.

p3.q: In what ways has urbanisation changed the relationship between neighbours in modern cities?
p3.a: Urbanisation has undeniably fostered anonymity. In high-rise apartment complexes, busy work schedules and private lifestyle choices mean that residents often keep to themselves, rarely knowing who lives next door. In contrast to rural hamlets where doors remain wide open, urban living prioritises privacy over communal solidarity, leading to weaker interpersonal bonds in metropolitan areas.

p3.q: To what extent should local governments encourage neighbourhood bonding activities?
p3.a: In my opinion, authorities ought to facilitate communal engagement rather than mandate it. By funding community centres or hosting green living workshops, councils can provide fertile ground for spontaneous interactions. However, participation must remain strictly voluntary, since over-regulating neighbourhood life could alienate citizens who value personal downtime after demanding working weeks.

mistakesVi: Dùng nhầm từ loại giữa 'neighbour' (danh từ chỉ người: người hàng xóm) và 'neighbourhood' (danh từ chỉ nơi chốn: khu phố, khu dân cư xung quanh).
Dịch từng từ cụm thành ngữ tiếng Việt như 'tối lửa tắt đèn có nhau' sang tiếng Anh một cách gượng gạo; nên dùng 'rely on each other in times of need' hoặc 'close support system'.
Phát âm sai trọng âm của từ 'neighbour' /ˈneɪbər/, thường nhấn âm hai hoặc phát âm đuôi thành /bɔːr/ do ảnh hưởng của mặt chữ.

outlineVi: Mở đầu: Giới thiệu ngắn gọn bản tin thú vị gần đây bạn đọc được (ví dụ: phát minh đột phá về công nghệ làm sạch rác thải nhựa đại dương của một nhóm kỹ sư trẻ).
Ý 1 (Nguồn & Thời điểm): Nêu rõ bạn tình cờ đọc được tin này ở đâu (trên trang tin tức khoa học uy tín) và vào thời gian nào (khoảng vài tuần trước khi lướt mạng buổi sáng).
Ý 2 (Nội dung chi tiết & Lý do thú vị): Giải thích nguyên lý hoạt động tóm tắt của sáng kiến, tại sao nó vượt trội so với các giải pháp trước đây và lý do thông tin này thu hút bạn.
Kết (Cảm xúc & Tác động): Chia sẻ cảm giác lạc quan và hy vọng về tương lai của môi trường sống, đồng thời truyền cảm hứng để bạn tự thay đổi thói quen dùng đồ nhựa.
news.sample:
A few weeks ago, while browsing a science journalism website, I stumbled across a truly fascinating piece of breaking news about a breakthrough in environmental engineering. The report highlighted an autonomous solar-powered vessel designed by a group of young Dutch engineers to capture plastic debris in rivers before it reaches the open ocean.

What caught my attention immediately was the practical ingenuity of the invention. Rather than deploying massive vessels that consume heavy fossil fuels, this system operates entirely on renewable energy and runs round the clock with minimal human intervention. Furthermore, initial trial runs in Southeast Asia showed that it could extract tons of synthetic waste within days.

I found this news extraordinarily encouraging. In an era dominated by alarming headlines about global warming and ecological crises, hearing about tangible, practical solutions felt like a breath of fresh air. It filled me with genuine optimism about our ability to reverse ecological damage through innovation, and it even inspired me to be more conscious of my own single-use plastic consumption.

p1.q: How do you usually get your daily news?
p1.a: I predominantly get my news through digital news aggregator apps on my smartphone. They provide concise digests and real-time alerts from reputable publishers, which fits neatly into my busy morning commute.

p1.q: Do you prefer reading international news or domestic news?
p1.a: I lean towards international news because I'm fascinated by global geopolitics and economic trends. However, I still glance through local headlines daily to stay informed about community developments and domestic public policies.

p1.q: Did you follow the news much when you were younger?
p1.a: Not really, as I found conventional newspapers rather tedious and abstract as a child. I mostly watched cartoons, only catching glimpses of the evening television news when my parents had it on.

p3.q: Why do many people prefer getting news from social media rather than traditional newspapers?
p3.a: Social media platforms offer immediacy and personalized algorithmic feeds that conventional newspapers simply cannot rival. Users receive bite-sized updates within seconds of an incident, accompanied by interactive commentary. However, this convenience often comes at the expense of journalistic rigor and objective fact-checking, making users vulnerable to sensationalism. Nonetheless, the fast-paced nature of modern life drives audiences toward these instant digital streams.

p3.q: To what extent should governments regulate fake news on digital platforms?
p3.a: In my view, state intervention is necessary to curb malicious misinformation, especially regarding public health or civil safety. Unchecked falsehoods can easily incite panic and erode social trust. Nevertheless, strict state oversight risks sliding into censorship and suppressing legitimate dissent. Therefore, rather than outright bans, authorities should mandate algorithmic transparency from tech giants while investing heavily in citizens' media literacy.

mistakesVi: Lỗi từ vựng và ngữ pháp: Nhầm lẫn giữa 'news' (danh từ không đếm được, luôn chia động từ số ít: 'The news is interesting') với danh từ đếm được, dẫn đến việc dùng sai như 'a news' hoặc 'many news' thay vì 'a piece of news' hay 'news stories'.

Lỗi diễn đạt thô: Dịch nguyên xi từ tiếng Việt 'xem tin tức trên tivi/mạng' thành 'see news' thay vì sử dụng các collocation tự nhiên như 'watch the news', 'read the news', hoặc 'follow current affairs'.

Lỗi hạn chế trường từ vựng: Lạm dụng cụm từ 'fake news' một cách tùy tiện mà không biết dùng các từ học thuật chuẩn xác hơn như 'misinformation' (tin sai lệch vô ý), 'disinformation' (tin sai lệch có chủ đích) hay 'sensationalism'.

online-shopping.sample: I'd like to share an experience of buying an ergonomic wireless keyboard online, which turned out to be an absolute bargain. I purchased it about three months ago from a flagship store on Shopee, one of the leading e-commerce platforms in Vietnam. I had been suffering from chronic wrist strain from typing all day, so I urgently needed an upgrade. Instead of visiting a bricks-and-mortar electronics store, I decided to shop online. Digital platforms allowed me to effortlessly compare specs, watch video demonstrations, and read hundreds of authentic customer reviews before committing. Furthermore, by using seasonal discount vouchers and free shipping codes, I saved nearly thirty percent compared to high-street retail prices. What made me exceptionally satisfied was not just the swift two-day delivery, but the impeccable build quality. The keys feel remarkably tactile and comfortable, instantly alleviating my joint pain. It arrived meticulously packaged with a genuine warranty seal. Overall, this seamless transaction reinforced my trust in online shopping and proved to be an invaluable investment for my remote work setup.

p1.q: How often do you buy things on the internet?
p1.a: I shop online quite frequently, roughly two or three times a month. It saves me considerable time, especially when restocking everyday essentials like skincare items or coffee beans via popular digital marketplaces.

p1.q: What kind of items do you usually purchase online?
p1.a: I mostly purchase tech accessories and non-perishable household goods. For instance, last week I bought a sturdy phone case and some books online because the pricing was far more competitive than physical shops.

p1.q: Have you ever encountered any problems when shopping online?
p1.a: Yes, on one occasion I ordered a cotton shirt that looked completely different from the website photos. The fabric felt flimsy, so I had to initiate a return request to retrieve my money.

p3.q: How has e-commerce transformed traditional retail businesses in recent years?
p3.a: Undoubtedly, e-commerce has forced traditional retailers to rethink their operating models. With digital platforms offering round-the-clock convenience and lower overhead costs, brick-and-mortar stores must now provide engaging customer experiences rather than just selling goods. For example, many apparel shops have created interactive showrooms where shoppers can test outfits before ordering them online. Ultimately, physical stores have had to integrate digital elements to survive.

p3.q: Do you think consumer spending habits have become more reckless because of online shopping?
p3.a: In my view, digital shopping certainly exacerbates impulsive spending. Algorithmic marketing, limited-time flash sales, and frictionless one-click payments lure consumers into purchasing goods they rarely require. In contrast, shopping in person requires deliberate effort and cash transactions, which encourage second thoughts. Consequently, people nowadays often accumulate clutter and blow their personal budgets far more easily than previous generations.

mistakesVi: Lặp lại cụm 'buy online' quá nhiều lần thay vì đa dạng hóa bằng 'shop online', 'order via digital storefronts' hay 'make online purchases'.

Nhầm lẫn giữa 'cash on delivery' (trả tiền khi nhận hàng) và các hình thức chuyển khoản số, dẫn tới việc dùng sai thuật ngữ khi mô tả phương thức thanh toán.
